locator: We present a systematic benchmark comparing Scanpy (CPU, 100 cores) against rapids-singlecell (GPU, 1-8 NVIDIA H100 80 GB) on the 1.3-million mouse brain cell dataset, evaluating speed, multi-GPU scal
claimed: Scanpy (CPU, 100 cores) vs rapids-singlecell (1-8 H100), five independent repeats
recomputed: CPU: SLURM --cpus-per-task=100 (slurm/cpu_benchmark.sh) su nodo con 224 CPU logiche (metadata.n_cpus=224 nei run GPU; l154: 112 core fisici) -> probabilmente 100 CPU logiche, non 100 core. 1 GPU solo fino a 100k (Table 4 l187). 2/4/8 GPU: PCA e neighbours eseguiti tutti su GPU 0 (adata.X mai convertito in Dask array, scripts/benchmark_multigpu.py; rsc 0.14.1 _pca.py usa Dask solo se X e' DaskArray). Ripetizioni sequenziali nello stesso processo Python: rep1 GPU 10k = 6.40 s vs media rep2-5 2.50 s.
source: tracks/F_work/f02_scrna_pow.py (PoW-1, PoW-2, PoW-6); slurm/*.sh; github scverse/rapids_singlecell v0.14.1 preprocessing/_pca.py
note: Il disegno dichiarato nell'abstract e' piu' forte di quello eseguito: '1-8 GPU' non corrisponde a calcolo distribuito, '100 cores' va dichiarato come CPU logiche, le ripetizioni non sono indipendenti (stesso processo, effetto rep1).

locator: The GPU pipeline achieved up to 120-fold end-to-end speedup at 1.3M cells (435 s vs 52,056 s on CPU), reducing a 14.5-hour analysis to 7.3 minutes.
claimed: up to 120-fold end-to-end speedup at 1.3M (435 s vs 52,056 s), 14.5 h -> 7.3 min
recomputed: Numeri ricalcolati: 52,056.21/435.18 = 119.62x; 14.46 h; 7.25 min (Results l183). Con 2 GPU 105.5x, con 4 GPU 107.0x. La differenza 2->8 GPU (58.1 s) sta tutta in data_loading (149.0 vs 90.6 s, lettura h5ad su CPU, nodo diverso). Il DE Wilcoxon e' il 93.5% del tempo CPU a 1.3M; senza DE lo speedup e' 7.9x (2 GPU) - 9.2x (8 GPU).
note: I numeri tornano, l'attribuzione no: '120x' dipende dal nodo/I-O del job a 8 GPU e quasi interamente dal DE su CPU. Cifra robusta: ~105x con 2 GPU, ~8-9x escludendo il DE.

locator: Biological concordance was high: HVG selection was identical (Jaccard = 1.0), PCA loadings perfectly correlated (Spearman |rho| = 1.0), and Leiden clustering concordance ranged from ARI = 0.908 to 0.9
claimed: HVG Jaccard 1.0, PCA |rho| 1.0, ARI 0.908-0.963
recomputed: results/concordance_10000_r1.json: ARI 0.9077 (r=1.0), 0.9317 (0.5), 0.9631 (1.5); HVG J=1.0; PCA mean |rho|=1.0 (Results l240-242). Solo a 10k e da un run del 2026-03-11 precedente al benchmark (CPU 40/45 cluster a r=1.0/1.5 contro 41/46 nei 5 run CPU del benchmark, deterministici; tempo GPU 16.9 s contro 3.3 s).
note: Numeri corretti, ma 'Biological concordance was high' e' presentato come proprieta' del benchmark mentre e' misurato a 10k su un run diverso da quello cronometrato. In letteratura ARI CPU-GPU ~0.5 su 50k-1.2M (Gardner 2025) e 0.54 a 1.3M (Nolet 2022).

locator: A memory-optimised pipeline processed 11.9 million cells on a single DGX H100 node, with CPU RAM as the binding constraint (GPU VRAM at 7.6% of capacity).
claimed: 11.9M cells on single DGX node; CPU RAM binding; VRAM 7.6%
recomputed: maxpower_11900000_8gpu_results.json: peak_ram 534.55 GB, peak_vram 48.84 GB -> 48.84/640 = 7.63% (Results l260-262, Table 5). Ma: i dati sopra 3.44M sono copie esatte del dataset CELLxGENE da 3,436,470 cellule (scripts/benchmark_maxpower.py, resize per replica), non 11.9M cellule distinte; la VRAM misura pool RMM riservati, non il fabbisogno; Results l262 dichiara non risolta l'attribuzione del fallimento a 12M.
note: Il vincolo 'CPU RAM' e' della pipeline scelta (preprocessing Scanpy su CPU), non dell'hardware; va dichiarato che le cellule oltre 3.4M sono duplicate.

locator: A differential expression benchmark at 3.4M cells showed pseudo-bulk aggregation 44x faster than cell-level t-test.
claimed: pseudo-bulk 44x faster than cell-level t-test at 3.4M
recomputed: de_benchmark_ttest_cpu.json time 5597.79 s / de_benchmark_pseudobulk.json time 127.47 s = 43.91x (Table 7 riporta 43.7x usando 128 s arrotondato). Results l321.
note: Confronto tra test e unita' statistiche diverse (2,431 pseudo-campioni vs 3.4M cellule): e' un tempo, non un fattore di accelerazione; 43.9 vs 43.7 per arrotondamento.

locator: We extended the benchmark to spatial transcriptomics on three 10x Visium platforms, achieving up to 51.6x end-to-end speedup (Visium HD 8 um) and 3,272x for co-occurrence analysis, with near-perfect s
claimed: 51.6x end-to-end (HD 8 um), 3,272x co-occurrence, rho >= 0.9995
recomputed: Con la convenzione rep2-5: totale 4068.40/78.79 = 51.6x; co-occurrence 3573.20/1.092 = 3271.5x (Table 8-9). Ma la rep1 esclusa come 'JIT warmup' e' quella in cui la CPU e' stata PIU' VELOCE: co-occurrence CPU r1 = 73.47 s contro 3570-3574 s in r2-5, con output identico bit a bit (.npy, max diff 0). Con tutte le ripetizioni: 41.5x e 2088x; rep1 da sola: 6.4x e 29.2x; CPU r1 vs GPU r2-5: 67x. Inoltre CPU calcola la co-occurrence su 7 cluster e GPU su 3 (carico diverso); concordanza della co-occurrence 'shape_mismatch'. rho >= 0.9995 confermato (Geary HD 8um 0.9995).
note: Le due cifre di testa dello spatial dipendono da una ripetizione esclusa con una giustificazione (warmup) che i dati contraddicono. Va spiegata la variabilita' 49x della CPU o riportato l'intervallo.

locator: Our benchmark demonstrates that rapids-singlecell on NVIDIA H100 GPUs delivers consistent, large-magnitude speedups over Scanpy for the standard scRNA-seq analysis pipeline, with high biological conco
claimed: consistent, large-magnitude speedups ... scalability to nearly 12 million cells
recomputed: Speedup end-to-end 8-46x (1 GPU 10k-100k), 19-25x (ibrida 50k-100k), 35x (500k), 105-120x (1.3M) (Table 4, l182-213); senza DE 3.7-10x. La scala a 11.9M usa un'altra pipeline e dati replicati (l256-281).
note: 'Consistent' non regge: lo speedup dipende dalla pipeline (1 GPU vs ibrida) e dal peso del DE; '12 million cells' sono copie di 3.4M.

locator: The extension to spatial transcriptomics shows that GPU advantages are even more pronounced for spatial-specific operations, with co-occurrence analysis achieving over three orders of magnitude speedu
claimed: GPU advantages even more pronounced for spatial-specific operations
recomputed: Spatial-specifiche HD 8um (rep2-5): co-occurrence 3272x (dipende dall'esclusione rep1), Moran/Geary 162x, spatial neighbours 1.0x, nhood enrichment 1.0x (Table 9 l351-366). In scRNA normalisation 173-329x (l217).
note: Solo la co-occurrence supera l'scRNA, ed e' la cifra fragile; due delle quattro operazioni spatial-specifiche non hanno GPU.

locator: These results reveal several important insights about GPU-accelerated single-cell analysis that merit detailed discussion.
claimed: frase di raccordo
recomputed: nessuna affermazione verificabile
note: Raccordo.

locator: The fundamental constraint underlying our results is that GPU speedup is inherently operation-specific and highly dependent on the computational structure of each step.
claimed: GPU speedup operation-specific
recomputed: Speedup per step 1 GPU (5 rip.): da 0.36x (leiden_0.5 a 10k) a 329x (normalisation a 10k) (Results l217-223, Fig. 1).
note: Sostenuto, con le riserve sullo 0.36x (vedi A0277).

locator: Normalisation and neighbour graph construction represent ideal GPU workloads, achieving speedups of 88-329x and 44-88x respectively, because they involve high arithmetic intensity and are trivially pa
claimed: Normalisation 88-329x, neighbours 44-88x, because high arithmetic intensity
recomputed: Results l217: normalisation 329x/206x/173x -> range 173-329x (ricalcolato 173.1-329.3; con rep2-5 115-137x); neighbours 44.3-88.1x (ok). Results l217 descrive la normalisation come 'only element-wise division and logarithm', cioe' bassa intensita' aritmetica (memory-bound).
note: Il limite inferiore 88x e' preso dai neighbours; il meccanismo invocato (alta intensita' aritmetica) e' l'opposto di quello di un'operazione element-wise. Il 329x dipende dalla rep1 lenta della CPU.

locator: In contrast, data loading from disk and Leiden clustering on small graphs show no GPU advantage or even a CPU advantage, but for different reasons.
claimed: data loading and Leiden on small graphs show no GPU advantage or CPU advantage
recomputed: Data loading 0.76-0.85x confermato (l223). Leiden a 10k: 0.36x solo per leiden_0.5 includendo rep1; escludendo rep1 1.12x; leiden_1.0 e 1.5 a 10k 1.36x e 1.60x anche con rep1; somma delle 3 risoluzioni 0.70x (5 rip.) e 1.31x (rep2-5).
note: Il vantaggio CPU nel Leiden a 10k e' un costo una tantum della prima chiamata cuGraph nella prima ripetizione, non una proprieta' dei grafi piccoli.

locator: For data loading the culprit is not bandwidth: at sub-gigabyte dataset sizes PCIe Gen5 (128 GB/s) is far from saturated and the transfer itself completes in milliseconds; what dominates the GPU-side c
claimed: data loading cost dominated by CUDA context initialisation and RMM pool allocation
recomputed: In scripts/benchmark_gpu.py init_rmm_pool() e gpu_warmup() sono chiamati PRIMA del time_step('data_loading'); Methods l83 dichiara lo stesso. Lo step cronometrato contiene read_h5ad + anndata_to_GPU.
note: La spiegazione attribuisce lo 0.76-0.85x a costi esclusi dal cronometro; la differenza nasce da anndata_to_GPU e dalla lettura. Contraddice i Methods.

locator: Leiden clustering on small graphs is limited by low arithmetic intensity: consistent with the roofline model [@Williams2009], cuGraph's constant-time overhead exceeds CPU's short runtime when the grap
claimed: Leiden on small graphs limited by low arithmetic intensity (roofline)
recomputed: Escludendo rep1, GPU Leiden a 10k e' piu' veloce della CPU (1.12x, 1.29x, 1.59x per r = 0.5, 1.0, 1.5). Inoltre CPU igraph usa n_iterations=2 (benchmark_cpu.py l239) e cuGraph max_iter=100 (rsc 0.14.1 tools/_clustering.py default n_iterations=100).
note: Il roofline non e' la spiegazione supportata dai dati: l'effetto e' di inizializzazione, e i due Leiden non fanno lo stesso lavoro.

locator: This heterogeneous speedup landscape has important practical implications for practitioners: GPU acceleration is most valuable for large datasets where the compute-heavy operations dominate overall ru
claimed: on small datasets the overhead of GPU operations may outweigh benefits
recomputed: A 10k la pipeline 1 GPU e' 12.0x (5 rip.) o 14.0x (rep2-5) piu' veloce; nessuna dimensione mostra la GPU piu' lenta end-to-end (Table 4).
note: Non osservato nei dati; Dicks et al. 2026 lo riportano sotto ~50k celle senza DE: va spiegato che qui il DE CPU domina anche a 10k (54.9% del tempo CPU).

locator: This step-level heterogeneity extends into multi-GPU scaling behaviour.
claimed: step-level heterogeneity extends into multi-GPU scaling
recomputed: Nessuno step e' stato distribuito tra GPU (vedi A0280); l'eterogeneita' tra 2/4/8 GPU sta nel data loading su CPU.
note: Cornice interpretativa senza base.

locator: The relatively modest 12% improvement from 2 to 8 GPUs at 1.3M cells reflects a fundamental constraint imposed by pipeline structure: only PCA and neighbour graph construction exploit distributed GPU
claimed: 12% improvement 2->8 GPUs because only PCA and neighbours exploit distributed GPU computation, remaining 95%
recomputed: Medie 5 rip. a 1.3M: totale 493.29 -> 435.18 s (-11.8% di tempo, 1.13x). PCA+neighbours 17.23 s (2 GPU) vs 17.01 s (8 GPU), delta 0.22 s; data_loading 148.99 vs 90.61 s, delta 58.38 s, cioe' circa il 100% della differenza totale (58.12 s). PCA e neighbours non distribuiti: adata.X e' un CuPy array su GPU 0, rsc.pp.pca usa Dask solo con DaskArray, rsc.pp.neighbors non ha percorso Dask. Quota non-PCA/neighbours: 96.2% (rep1) / 96.1% (media), non 95%.
source: tracks/F_work/f02_steps_2v8_1300000.csv; scripts/benchmark_multigpu.py righe 320-380; rapids_singlecell v0.14.1 _pca.py e _neighbors/__init__.py
note: Il 12% non e' scaling multi-GPU ma una differenza di I/O tra nodi/job concorrenti (driver 535.247.01 per 2/4 GPU, 535.183.01 per 8 GPU). Il diario del progetto (CLAUDE.md) scrive per la pipeline standard 'PCA: Single-GPU truncated SVD' e 'Other 7 GPUs sat idle'.

locator: This imbalance represents a classic manifestation of Amdahl's law [@Amdahl1967], where the non-parallelised fraction dominates overall speedup.
claimed: classic manifestation of Amdahl's law
recomputed: Fit T(N)=a+b/N sui 15 run 2/4/8 GPU a 1.3M: totale b=136.6 s (IC95 57-216) ma tutto dal data_loading (b=141.4); totale meno data_loading b=-4.75 s (IC95 -51.9, 42.4), frazione parallela ~0. Delta 2->4 = 6.7 s e delta 4->8 = 51.5 s: con Amdahl il primo dovrebbe essere il doppio del secondo.
note: Non c'e' frazione parallela da stimare: Amdahl con p~0 descrive l'assenza di parallelismo, non un limite strutturale. Riferimento Amdahl1967 DOI dal bib, non aperto in questa sessione.

locator: Future frameworks could address this bottleneck by distributing preprocessing operations (e.g., chunked QC and normalisation across GPUs) and parallelising Leiden clustering across partitions, but suc
claimed: distributing preprocessing would require substantial modifications to Scanpy architecture
recomputed: rapids-singlecell v0.14.1 ha gia' rami Dask per normalize_total, log1p (_normalize.py) e pca (_pca.py); la documentazione stable elenca anche calculate_qc_metrics, filter_cells/genes, highly_variable_genes, scale. Nolet et al. 2022 distribuivano filtering e normalisation su 8 V100 (272 -> 60 s a 1.3M).
source: github scverse/rapids_singlecell v0.14.1 _normalize.py, _pca.py; rapids-singlecell.scverse.org stable out_of_core.md; Nolet 2022 Table 1
note: L'opzione esisteva nello stack usato; non e' stata attivata.

locator: A practical consequence for resource allocation follows from this constraint: because the marginal speedup of adding GPUs to a single run is only approximately 12%, a DGX H100 node is more efficiently
claimed: 8 independent single-GPU workers with near-linear throughput scaling
recomputed: Throughput concorrente non misurato. I job 2 e 4 GPU girati in contemporanea sullo stesso nodo (driver 535.247.01, timestamp sovrapposti) hanno data_loading 149.0 e 135.1 s contro 90.6 s del job 8 GPU da solo su altro nodo: contesa di I/O gia' osservata. Lo speedup normalizzato per costo (f03) favorisce comunque meno GPU per job (2 GPU 34-175x vs 8 GPU 10-50x).
note: Direzione plausibile (meno GPU per job), ma 'near-linear' e' contraddetto dalla contesa osservata: il 75% del tempo e' preprocessing CPU che si contende core e disco.

locator: This is a non-obvious but important takeaway for groups operating shared GPU infrastructure: the capital-intensive DGX platform delivers its greatest return when treated as a cluster of eight H100 wor
claimed: DGX delivers greatest return as cluster of eight H100 workstations
recomputed: Nessuna misura di throughput, costo o ritorno; vedi A0283.
note: Affermazione di economia senza dati.

locator: Related to this, most of the practical value of the GPU speedup is accessible without a DGX at all.
claimed: most of the practical value accessible without a DGX
recomputed: A 500k e 1.3M la pipeline single-GPU non e' stata misurata (Table 4 l187); la variante ibrida con n_gpus=1 non e' stata eseguita.
note: Plausibile perche' tutto il calcolo GPU e' gia' su GPU 0, ma non misurato.

locator: At dataset sizes below 500,000 cells the full standard pipeline fits on a single H100 GPU, and the memory-optimised variant described here extends single-GPU feasibility to 1.3M cells and beyond.
claimed: below 500,000 cells fits on a single H100; memory-optimised variant extends single-GPU feasibility to 1.3M and beyond
recomputed: Single-GPU misurato solo a 10k/50k/100k; soglia tra 100k e 500k non determinata. La variante memory-optimised e' stata eseguita solo a 8 GPU (tutti i file maxpower_*_8gpu; PCA covarianza distribuita su 8 GPU).
note: 'Single-GPU feasibility to 1.3M and beyond' non e' stata testata.

locator: Single H100 GPUs are readily rentable on commercial cloud platforms at approximately USD 2 to 4 per hour, so the 120x speedup at 1.3M cells reported here (reducing a 14.5-hour CPU analysis to 7.3 minu
claimed: single H100 USD 2-4/h; 120x at 1.3M -> well under one dollar
recomputed: Il 120x richiede 8 GPU: 8 x 435.18 s x 2-4 USD/GPU-h = 1.93-3.87 USD. Con 2 GPU (105x): 0.55-1.10 USD. Una GPU sola non e' stata misurata a 1.3M. Prezzi letti: 1.99-4.29 USD/GPU-h (neocloud) e 6.88-12.29 (hyperscaler) (intuitionlabs, agg. 2026-10-11); Lambda 3.99.
note: La frase combina il tempo a 8 GPU con il prezzo di 1 GPU. Il range 2-4 USD vale solo per neocloud.

locator: Access to a full DGX is therefore not a prerequisite for adopting these methods; the results are directly relevant to individual researchers and small groups with pay-as-you-go cloud budgets.
claimed: access to a DGX not a prerequisite; directly relevant to pay-as-you-go budgets
recomputed: Dipende da A0285-A0287 (single-GPU a 1.3M non misurato).
note: Riformulare come ipotesi.

locator: The biological outputs of GPU and CPU pipelines show high agreement despite computing on fundamentally different architectures and hardware.
claimed: biological outputs show high agreement
recomputed: Misurato solo a 10k (concordance_10000_r1.json).
note: Generalizzazione oltre il disegno.

locator: The perfect concordance on HVG selection (Jaccard = 1.000) and PCA loadings (Spearman rho = 1.000) reflects the deterministic nature of these operations given identical numerical inputs.
claimed: HVG Jaccard 1.000 and PCA rho 1.000
recomputed: concordance_10000_r1.json: hvg jaccard 1.0, pca mean_abs_spearman_rho 1.0 (Results l240). In piu': hash della lista HVG identico CPU vs 1 GPU a 10k, 50k, 100k (f02_determinism.csv).
note: Sostenuto; l'identita' HVG si estende a 100k (dato utile da aggiungere). 'Identical numerical inputs' e' improprio: l'input GPU proviene da un preprocessing diverso.

locator: The adjusted Rand indices for Leiden clustering range from 0.908 to 0.963 across different resolutions, entirely consistent with the algorithm's inherent stochasticity across implementations (igraph v
claimed: ARI 0.908-0.963 consistent with inherent stochasticity across implementations
recomputed: ARI ricalcolati ok. Ma: CPU Leiden identico nei 5 run a ogni N (1 hash); GPU identico a 10k; differenza di configurazione sistematica (igraph n_iterations=2 vs cuGraph max_iter=100); concordanza da run del 2026-03-11 (CPU 40/45 cluster vs 41/46 nel benchmark). Duo 2020 valuta 14 metodi in R, non igraph vs cuGraph.
source: tracks/F_work/f02_determinism.csv; scripts/benchmark_cpu.py l236-240; results/concordance_10000_r1.json; OpenAlex Duo 2020
note: La differenza e' implementativa e di configurazione, non stocastica.

locator: Floating-point non-associativity in GPU parallel reductions contributes negligibly to observed differences, as the dominant source of variation is the Leiden algorithm's non-deterministic vertex order
claimed: FP non-associativity negligible; dominant source is Leiden vertex ordering
recomputed: Nessun esperimento separa le due fonti (es. Leiden CPU sul grafo GPU, o semi diversi a parita' di grafo). A 10k la GPU e' deterministica tra ripetizioni.
note: Affermazione causale senza esperimento; proposto PoW-H.

locator: This level of concordance is reassuring for practitioners: it indicates that GPU-accelerated and CPU-based analyses remain interchangeable for biological interpretation and conclusions.
claimed: GPU and CPU analyses interchangeable for biological interpretation
recomputed: Solo 10k. A >=50k le etichette GPU cambiano tra ripetizioni con lo stesso seme (fino a 4 partizioni diverse in 5 run a 1.3M, r=1.5; numero di cluster 82-84) e il numero di cluster GPU diverge dalla CPU (1.3M r=1.0: CPU 75, GPU 67-70). Gardner 2025: ARI ~0.5 e 'they are not interchangeable'; Nolet 2022: ARI 0.54 a 1.3M.
note: Conclusione piu' forte del disegno e in contrasto non discusso con la letteratura citata.

locator: Perhaps most importantly, our findings reveal that CPU-side memory pressure during preprocessing, not GPU VRAM, is the binding constraint on scalability at extreme scale.
claimed: CPU-side memory pressure, not GPU VRAM, is the binding constraint
recomputed: Coerente con Results l260-265 per questa pipeline (scale OOM a 13.7M, HVG OOM a 14M). ScaleSC elabora 13M cellule su una sola A100; Dicks 2026 100M su 8 B300 con Dask out-of-core.
note: Vincolo della pipeline (preprocessing Scanpy in memoria), non dell'analisi GPU in generale.

locator: This challenges the common intuition that GPU memory availability limits GPU-accelerated analysis.
claimed: challenges the common intuition
recomputed: Nessuna fonte citata per 'common intuition'.
note: Retorica; togliere o citare.

locator: At the maximum testable scale of 11.9 million cells, aggregate GPU VRAM remained flat at 49 GB (7.6% of the 640 GB total) while stable peak CPU RAM reached 535 GB.
claimed: VRAM flat at 49 GB (7.6% of 640 GB), peak RAM 535 GB at 11.9M
recomputed: maxpower_11900000: peak_vram 48.84 GB, 48.84/640 = 7.63%; peak_ram 534.55 GB (Results l262, Table 5).
note: Numeri ok; la VRAM include i pool RMM (2 GB/worker) e misura riservato, non fabbisogno.

locator: Critically, the 12M-cell failure did not occur because CPU RAM was exhausted on average (535 GB is only 30% of the 1.8 TB job allocation): it occurred because transient memory spikes during individual
claimed: failure occurred because transient memory spikes briefly multiplied the working set past the cgroup limit
recomputed: 535/1800 = 29.7% ok. Nessuna misura dei picchi: Results l262 'treat the attribution ... as unresolved'; Table 6 stimata; strumentazione solo tra step e solo processo padre (l111).
note: La frase afferma come causa cio' che i Risultati dichiarano non risolto (pur con 'most plausibly').

locator: The bottleneck is therefore not "RAM being full" in the usual sense but a set of short-lived peaks that the scanpy preprocessing stack is structured to create.
claimed: short-lived peaks that the scanpy preprocessing stack is structured to create
recomputed: Non misurato (vedi A0297).
note: Asserzione causale non sostenuta.

locator: Substantial further gains in capacity could be realised through preprocessing frameworks that avoid these transient peaks (e.g., reference-only `adata.raw`, streaming Leiden on partitions, chunked spa
claimed: gains via avoiding transient peaks; VRAM heavily underutilised
recomputed: Il Leiden e' escluso come colpevole lato host (l262), eppure 'streaming Leiden' e' tra i rimedi; la VRAM misurata e' dominata dai pool.
note: Suggerimenti non collegati ai dati.

locator: The capacity limit is more accurately described as a function of cells x HVGs rather than cell count alone, because the dense scaled matrix materialised during preprocessing must occupy one contiguous
claimed: capacity ~ cells x HVGs; 20M cells at 1,000 HVGs and 4M at 5,000
recomputed: Matrice densa a 11.9M x 2000 x 4 B = 95.2 GB = 17.8% del picco 534.55 GB. Anche con capacita' inversamente proporzionale agli HVG: 23.8M (1000) e 4.76M (5000). Con il bilancio di Table 6 (36.9 kB/cella non-HVG): 13.1M e 9.4M.
